notes.summary: Constructed exact compact algebraic rational PL extensions, support-controlled partitions and same-bundle FS differences. These give an algebraic representation first for supplied continuous contact metrics, avoiding the arbitrary-formal-line-bundle algebraization gap. Arbitrary weak metric approximation is not established.
notes.detailedSummary: For reduced irreducible projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields, finite rational selected unit-log weights admit exact compact algebraic PL extensions through original-ring localization, compact norm-image subdivision and saturation cutoffs. Finite signed tests decompose into genuine FS metrics in one actual ample bundle with the original cocycle. A supplied globally glued continuous rational contact metric is first represented algebraically using BJ flag ideals; ordinary-neighborhood curve tests then establish nefness of its represented Laurent model. Same-class approximation and an exact Gauss cutoff give genuine membership. All combined applications remain unverified proof drafts.
notes.text:
Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible projective, and actual ample rational line bundles. The contact hypothesis is binding: on ordinary point neighborhoods a continuous weight is a finite rational-affine selection in analytic-unit logarithms, and at each image point it has an affine support below it and equal there with the SAME constant. Finite-floor maxima handle zero coordinates by deleting inactive branches. This does not assert an unrestricted positive-current converse.

The new compact extension construction retains the original ring. For a very ample H and a nonzero section s, section localization gives Γ(D(s),O_X)=colim_m H⁰(X,mH)/s^m without normality. On a finite affine trivializing cover this is module localization; the finite matching equalizers commute with filtered localization. If inverted functions are τ_i/s^{d_i}, a=s∏τ_i gives precisely D(a)=D(s)∩⋂D(τ_i). Every regular function on that chart is F/a^m for an appropriate global section F.

Let b_F be the ideal locally generated by a section's coefficient. Its logarithmic ideal norm equals its section norm for the canonical trivial metric, evaluated in a valuation-ring center frame. Consequently A_{F,N}=max(log|b_F|,-N) is an actual global BJ rational PL function, represented by a flag ideal after clearing rational denominators. If f=F/a^m is a unit on a compact W, clipping levels below the minima of the two section logarithms give log|f|=A_{F,N}-mA_{a,N'} exactly on a neighborhood of W.

Analytic units can first be replaced by regular functions with identical norms on smaller compact rational domains. Published Ducros Theorem 3.2's algebraic reduction localizes at a nonvanishing denominator h and uses density of functions b/h^r in the original affinoid algebra. Choose g with ||f-g||_W<min_W|f|. The ultrametric inequality gives |g|=|f| everywhere on W, also after complete field extension. This is an application on its specified rational domains, not polynomial density on arbitrary analytic opens.

Choose compact rational neighborhoods inside the supplied unit charts, with rational strict margins. They are Γ-strict for Γ=exp(Q). Ducros 3.2 gives finite rational polytope complexes as their unit-log images, of dimension at most dim X. Refine by branch-equality hyperplanes. On each relative open convex cell the distinct affine values have fixed order; continuity makes the selected expression class locally constant, hence constant. Its affine value extends to the closed cell.

To extend that selected function, put the finite rational complex T inside a rational box, cut by its finitely many defining hyperplanes, and barycentrically subdivide. T and every affine piece become subcomplexes. Give T's vertices their prescribed rational values, box-boundary vertices zero, and other vertices arbitrary rational values. Affine interpolation, followed by zero outside the box, is a continuous finite rational PL extension E. It is a difference of convex rational PL functions: adding C∑|h_j| for the finitely many wall hyperplanes, with sufficiently large rational C, makes every normal gradient jump nonnegative. Generic-line restrictions are convex, and continuity handles intersections. Both convex functions are maxima of finitely many rational affine expressions. Substituting the exact global PL logarithms above therefore produces an actual global algebraic PL extension.

Support is controlled without multiplying variable PL functions. For compact K⊂U choose a continuous bump b=1 near K supported compactly in U. BJ PL density gives rational PL p with ||p-b||<1/8. Then χ=min(1,max(0,2p-1/2)) is one near K and Supp χ⊂{p≥1/4} compactly contained in U. If local extensions E_i agree with f on neighborhoods of Supp χ_i and some χ_i=1 near each point of K, then max_i(E_i-C(1-χ_i)) equals f near K for a sufficiently large rational C: positive cutoffs lie in agreement charts; zero-cutoff branches are suppressed by the compact bounds. A further cutoff η=1 near K gives the compact signed extension max(-Bη,min(Bη,E)), with |extension|≤Bη, equal to f near K and zero near the complement of U. Products such as ηE are not used.

For a finite cover choose compact shrinkings and these χ_i. Set ρ_1=χ_1 and ρ_i=min(χ_i,1-∑_{j<i}ρ_j). Induction gives ∑_{j≤i}ρ_j=min(1,∑_{j≤i}χ_j); thus the ρ_i are nonnegative rational PL, subordinate with compact support, and sum to one. No variable denominator occurs.

Every finite signed PL list decomposes in one actual ample class. BJ2.25–2.26 gives a_i=c_i⁺q_i⁺−c_i⁻q_i⁻ with q_i⁺,q_i⁻ in H(H). Choose common rational R≥c_i⁺,c_i⁻ and replace each term by c_i q_i+(R-c_i)0 in H(RH). Tensor-product generating sections verify FS membership. Both metrics use the same RH, canonical reference and original cleared transition functions g_{αβ}^{NR}; their difference is exactly a_i. Numerical nefness alone is not substituted for these actual metrics.

There is consequently an algebraic-first bridge for an ALREADY glued continuous rational contact metric on ample L. In standard very ample frames its canonical reference weight is a finite logarithmic maximum with a zero floor. The preceding local extensions and maximum-penalty gluing show that its canonical potential φ is globally in BJ PL(X). BJ2.7/2.31 represents φ by an actual test-configuration bundle with generic bundle L, taking relative integral closure inside the original generic fiber. Completing at t over K=k((t)), |t|=e⁻¹, gives precisely the pulled metric: for flag ideals its norm is the maximum over separate ideal generators a_λt^{-λ}. Thus the algebraic model exists before nefness is tested.

This avoids the unchecked arbitrary-bundle algebraization step: GM2.4 algebraizes a formal blowup ideal, whereas GM2.6 cites GK17 Proposition8.13 for the separate formal-line-bundle converse. That latter full proof is not in the authorized caches. No arbitrary formal bundle is algebraized in this construction.

For any smooth analytic curve map over a completed algebraic closure of K, a pulled contact support h_x=∑a_j log|f_j|+C is harmonic by Thuillier2.3.21. If b-h has a local maximum M for harmonic h, then h_x-h≤b-h≤M with equality at x. The harmonic maximum principle makes h_x-h=M nearby and forces b-h=M nearby. Thuillier3.1.12 gives subharmonicity. Each continuous approximant is restricted first; Thuillier3.1.8(ii) is then used for decreasing limits, with bounded floors excluding the identically-minus-infinity alternative.

The metric is already represented PL. GR5.1/5.4 therefore gives semipositivity on ordinary point neighborhoods. GM3.11 tests every entire proper residual curve at a point reducing to its generic point, retaining its interior condition and a common dominating model. GM3.5/3.3 tests nefness on the represented model and detects it before extension. Positivity is not inferred from a Laurent G-cover alone, and GR Remark1.8's unknown current converse is not used.

BE7.8 interpolates the nef model with an ample model of the SAME generic L_K and gives uniform pure FS approximation. Expand its sections s_j=∑_{r≥r₀}t^r f_{jr} in H⁰(X,mL). At an independent-variable Gauss lift the potential is m⁻¹max_{j,r}(log||f_{jr}||_{mh₀}−r). Every k-section has canonical norm at most one. The finite continuous potential on compact X_an has a finite lower bound, so all sufficiently large r terms lie uniformly below it and can be removed EXACTLY. The remaining coefficient sections generate; a common zero would contradict that lower bound. They are actual sections of the original mL with rational weights. Uniform errors survive restriction, yielding genuine continuous membership over k. Errors ε_j=4⁻ʲ and shifts B_j=2∑_{i≥j}ε_i give a decreasing same-class FS sequence.

Primary applications and pertinent proof bodies are pinned at BJ1801.08229v4 LF938–1089,1309–1352,1420–1455; published Ducros LF2077–2155; GM1608.08030v3 LF249–295,633–782; GR2503.05513v1 LF489–926; Thuillier tel-00010990v1 LF3580–3627,3730–3741,3783–3820,3860–3907; BE1805.01016v3 LF2281–2363. Coordinates are inclusive one-based UTF-8 decode/split('\n'). These are source-based, unverified combined applications, not independent correctness certificates.

notes.summary: Reconstructed genuine bounded collars and compact signed IBP with outside-support cancellation. A support-controlled telescope gives exact raw mixed mass, followed by comparison, atom-based local domination and EP-based smooth membership for the specified contact class.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1 and primary genuine global pairings, bounded local decreasing contact tuples admit shared collars in an actual ample bundle. Their canonical potentials include the reference p, and their raw products retain A^n scaling. Compact signed tests decompose in one ample class; the positive measures cancel outside their support rather than individually vanishing. Symmetric global pairings yield compact IBP. Rational PL partitions then prove raw mass, comparison and domination without assuming local/global equality. EP and continuous-majorant nets establish first genuine membership; known smooth characteristic-zero EP supplies the smooth instance. Singular EP is not established.
notes.text:
Use n1's exact extensions, contact metric representation and actual same-bundle positivity. Retain its field, variety and rational contact hypotheses. The following arguments do not assume the desired weak/global theorem.

Around a tested point in the common neighborhood of a finite bounded tuple, original-ring localization constructs an actual FS local reference v on a fixed ample H. Its compact Q={v≤0} lies inside that neighborhood, and P={v≤−ε} contains the point in its interior. Appending a complete very ample section system makes the ratios generate the original principal-chart ring. If q is the tensor denominator, v=q⁻¹max(qλ,log|F_j/a^m|−C_j); the thresholds are C_j, not qC_j. Write v=h₀+p, with p the actual global FS potential and ω=c₁(H).

Let u_{ij} decrease to bounded local contact limits u_i, including a bounded test if needed. Choose rational M bounding the limits near Q and rational A with Aε>2M+2. Put h=Av+M+1. On P, h<−M; on the compact outer strip v≥−1/(2A), h≥M+1/2. The closed sets {u_{ij}≥M+1/4} there decrease to the empty set. Compactness supplies one common eventual tail strictly below h on the WHOLE strip. This does not assert uniform convergence to a discontinuous limit.

Set Ψ_{ij}=max(u_{ij}−h,0) on Q and zero outside, and Φ_{ij}=p+Ψ_{ij}/A. Their actual weights on H are A⁻¹max(u_{ij}−M−1,Av) inside, and v on the whole reference-winning collar and outside. n1 proves genuine same-bundle membership after clearing A. Their bounded decreasing limits Φ_i are genuine finite energy. On the inner open, u_i=AΦ_i+Ah₀+M+1, so dd^c u_i=A(ω+dd^cΦ_i). The reference p cannot be omitted. Define local products by A^n times the restricted genuine RAW mixed measure.

Continuous products agree with the actual local continuous theory by BJ7.23/7.42 and BE8.18, retaining fundamental cycles. For decreasing bounded inputs use genuine BJ7.19/7.21. Independence uses a third smaller shared collar: continuous products of one sequence agree in its old and smaller collars at every stage; both genuine limits therefore agree against compact tests. In the shared collar different sequences have the SAME explicit global limit max(u_i−h,0), zero outside. Their genuine measures agree. This proves independence of sequences, collars and references and permits gluing.

For a bounded decreasing test its inner weight is a genuine decreasing potential plus a fixed continuous reference. Genuine weighted convergence handles the former; weak convergence against compact cutoffs handles the latter. The correct BJ7.21 scalar identity is the test-containing pairing MINUS the zero-test pairing, as at LF4108–4113. The reverse signs at LF4119–4123 are a printed error. Translate below zero and use the positive weighted-measure lemma. Signed differences are passed separately; their difference need not decrease. CLD8.7.2 is used only for its literal continuous locally-uniform premise.

Compact signed IBP now follows from actual global pairings. Let a be a global rational PL test supported on K compactly contained in U, and let u₀,u₁,…,u_{n−1} be bounded local contact limits near K. Choose one collar for the tuple and a further cutoff equal to one near K. Decompose a=q⁺−q⁻ in the same actual ample RH using n1. The associated positive global mixed measures need NOT individually be supported in K. Their DIFFERENCE is: outside K, q⁺=q⁻, so genuine mixed locality makes their measures equal. This cancellation is retained before outside contributions are discarded.

Use n1 to extend Ah₀+M+1 to a compact signed global PL G₀ matching near K. Then F₀=AΦ₀+G₀ is a global signed finite-energy function equal to u₀ near K. Its zero-class curvature equals dd^c u₀ there: first verify matching-reference cancellation for continuous collar stages, then pass each positive genuine mixed limit. The symmetric global pairing with zero-class entries (0,a) and (0,F₀) gives

∫_U a dd^c u₀∧∏_{i=1}^{n−1}dd^c u_i = ∫_U u₀ dd^c a∧∏_{i=1}^{n−1}dd^c u_i.

The left test vanishes outside K; the signed measure on the right vanishes there by the preceding cancellation. All remaining functions are bounded over a compact set and all measures finite signed Radon. The other collar scaling factors are retained. Equivalently pass continuous IBP term by term using weighted convergence; total variation is bounded by the sum of fixed positive raw intersection masses. Neither a locally-uniform discontinuous limit nor a decreasing signed difference is assumed.

For raw global mass, let φ be bounded and locally contact-psh relative to an actual rational semipositive reference on L. Write T=ω+dd^cφ, T₀=ω, and S=∑_{j=0}^{n−1}T^jT₀^{n−1−j}, interpreted through the established local products. Choose n1's finite subordinate rational PL partition ρ_i. In each chart use the SAME reference g_i for φ+g_i and g_i. Subtract their compact IBP identities:

∫ρ_i(T^n−T₀^n)=∫φ dd^cρ_i∧S.

The signed measures have controlled chart supports and their bounded weighted integrals agree on overlaps. Sum the finite identities. Locally, ∑dd^cρ_i∧S=dd^c1∧S=0. Therefore ∫T^n=(L^n)=V. Replacing one factor at a time proves mixed mass (L₁⋯L_n). With a noncanonical reference, use its actual local weights in both subtracted terms; its genuine reference product has the same intersection mass. Mass has been proved, not imposed by normalization.

Shared collars satisfy Ψ_max(u,v)=max(Ψ_u,Ψ_v), and the floors are inactive on the inner open. Genuine BJ7.40 gives strict winning-locus locality, including Borel winning sets. Equal raw masses, positivity and the displaced maximum max(φ,ψ−ε) imply the comparison inequality ∫_{φ<ψ}T_ψ^n≤∫_{φ<ψ}T_φ^n after ε decreases to zero.

Divisorial order is independent of density arguments. If φ≤ψ at every BJ divisorial point, their shared genuine truncations are ordered inside Q and both zero outside. BJ4.22 orders them everywhere; recovering their inactive-floor weights proves the original order near the tested point.

For domination, fix a divisorial v. BJ1.20 realizes it as a central component of a relatively integrally closed test configuration. Dominate the trivial configuration and use BJ2.33 to give the ORIGINAL L an ample model there. Its genuine FS potential b has positive raw atom b_E(ℒ|_E)^n at v, with b_E=ord_E(t). No inverse Dirac equation is needed. Translate b so b<φ uniformly. For rational t>0 put φ_t=(1−t)φ+tb. Mixed positivity gives T_{φ_t}^n≥t^nT_b^n. If φ≤ψ almost everywhere for T_ψ^n, then φ_t<ψ there. Comparison and raw mass give V≤∫_{φ_t<ψ}T_{φ_t}^n≤V. Thus the complement has zero mass; the positive atom forces φ_t(v)<ψ(v). Let t decrease to zero and apply divisorial order. This proves bounded local domination before local/global equality.

Finally assume genuine ample EP. For bounded usc locally psh φ, use the directed decreasing NET of continuous majorants with common bounds and finite minima. Compact Hausdorff separation proves that their infimum is φ; no sequence is assumed. EP gives continuous genuine p_j=P(f_j). Their same-bundle rational FS approximants, shifted into decreasing sequences, put them in the stated local class. BJ13.1 under its explicit EP hypothesis gives f_j=p_j almost everywhere for T_{p_j}^n. Hence φ≤p_j there; LOCAL domination yields φ≤p_j≤f_j everywhere. Genuine decreasing closure proves φ is genuine.

BJ5.20 supplies EP on smooth projective varieties in characteristic zero, giving smooth local/global equality for this class. Bounded floors extend it to nontrivial unbounded inputs. For a rational nef bundle with a supplied actual semipositive reference, add εA with its specified FS reference, apply the smooth ample result, and use varying-class closure. The weights are literally the original weight plus εh_A; numerical nefness alone does not identify them. This establishes first membership BEFORE BJ12.18.

Evidence: BJ1801.08229v4 LF3980–4148,4519–4607,2488–2541,1420–1455,2980–3065,6304–6372; CLD1204.6277v2 LF10432–10449; BE1805.01016v3 LF2611–2779,3125–3202. Wu2609.27610v1 LF1331–1537 is retained as the original compact-IBP/mass argument being reconstructed. They establish the stated smooth gate, not singular EP or the original singular equation.

notes.summary: Derived smooth weak UPPER-growth AFS regularization and exact principal-open removal after first membership, with the geometric witness construction explicit. Independently audited canonical nonflat norm weights and whole-base finite AFS formulas; the general weak radial trace application remains unfinished.
notes.detailedSummary: With a smooth ample-boundary compactification and smooth projective domination of the one original proper birational contact witness, n2 supplies genuine membership for whole-floor nef truncations. BJ5.13 is applied only to a smooth target with approaching target-side EP; BJ12.18 follows membership. Exact localization and low complete-system branches retain original affine generators. Expanding collars yield controlled upper bounds. Smooth tail envelopes remove logarithmic penalties, and divisorial order on the original resolved witness identifies every removed-set value. Separately, generic norm laws specialize across nonflat fibers; Cayley–Hamilton forces strictly positive integer character exponents, giving canonical weights totaling generic degree and exact whole-base Gauss formulas. Those finite formulas do not by themselves identify arbitrary weak traces at nonflat points.
notes.text:
Use n1 and n2 with their retained rational contact class. Let Y be smooth irreducible affine over the same arbitrary algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. A weak u is supplied with ONE proper birational witness whose pullback is locally a decreasing contact limit, and u is finite at the generic trivial seminorm. Retain the standard characteristic-zero compactification, projective domination/Chow and resolution background yielding a smooth projective X containing Y, an effective ample boundary, and a smooth projective map π̄:Z→X dominating that same witness over Y. These geometric constructions are explicit premises of this deduction; no full proof or pinned Stacks webpage proof of them is claimed here.

The boundary sign is essential. A boundary blowup has effective exceptional E with −E relatively ample. If D is the previous ample boundary, then mπ*D−E is ample for sufficiently large m, effective and positive on every new boundary component. Iteration retains precisely the complement of Y as support. Choose very ample B=O(rD), boundary section s and rational complete FS metric h=h₀+p, shifted so g=−log||s||_h=g₀+p≥1. It exhausts Y and tends to infinity at the boundary. Original-ring section localization writes each original affine generator and every regular branch of an AFS bound as F/s^d, giving log|F/s^d|≤dg+C_F. Thus the assumed UPPER growth u≤H+C gives u≤Ag for rational A. The printed lower-growth convention is not used.

For c>1 rational and M<0, define relative to the actual nef reference cAπ̄*h the potential Ψ_M=max(π̄*u−cAπ̄*g,M) over Y and M elsewhere. Its nonfloor branch is at most −(c−1)Aπ̄*g, so it has a WHOLE constant boundary collar. The actual local weights are contact limits with that fixed pulled reference. n2's smooth nef local/global theorem gives genuine membership. Let M decrease to minus infinity; generic finiteness keeps the limit nontrivial.

The canonical potential is Q_M=Ψ_M+cAπ̄*p. Apply BJ5.13 to the SMOOTH target X in class cAc₁(B); its approaching larger TARGET-side ample classes have known smooth EP. The descended genuine Q equals u−cAg+cAp=u−cAg₀ on Y and minus infinity on its boundary, by literal pullback equality and analytic surjectivity. Only now use BJ12.18(iii) and Example3.9 to get a decreasing rational FS sequence on the SAME cAB. In the boundary-section frame its weights decrease exactly to u. Append a constant branch and a complete high very ample section system with low rational weights dominated by each continuous metric on compact X_an. Their ratios retain the original affine generators and change no value. This proves actual upper-growth AFS regularization under the stated geometric witness construction, rather than treating BJ12.18 as a membership theorem.

Controlled bounds can be obtained before singular EP. Compactify an actual AFS reference g by clearing its positive slopes and embedding with their integer powers AND all original generators at dominated low weights. Its standard chart is the original Y. For v_j decreasing to v≤g choose C_r decreasing to minus infinity, R_r increasing with R_r>2−C_r, and indices j_r with v_{j_r}<g+1 on {g≤R_r}; compact decreasing superlevel-set emptiness supplies them. Define φ_r=max(v_{j_r}−2g,C_r) inside that compact set and C_r outside. Whole collars and n1 give genuine metrics in twice the actual reference bundle. On the expanding annulus the new first branch is at most 1−g≤1−R_{r−1}<C_{r−1}, so the sequence decreases globally. Its limit is v−2g on Y and minus infinity at the boundary. Genuine same-class regularization gives actual AFS w_r decreasing to v with w_r≤2g+B for one B. No singular EP is used here.

For principal-open removal, let f≠0 and v be AFS-regularizable on Y_f with upper bound from Y. For rational c>0 take g_c=max(g,−(c/3)log|f|), an actual exhaustion of the localized ORIGINAL ring retaining f⁻¹. Controlled approximants satisfy

w_i+c log|f| ≤ max(2g+c log|f|,(c/3)log|f|)+B.

Near each removed point the right side tends to minus infinity. Floors D_i decreasing to minus infinity make b_i=max(w_i+c log|f|,D_i) continuous contact functions on Y, equal to D_i on an actual neighborhood of each removed point. One AFS h≥1 dominates all b_i. Whole-floor collars put b_i−2h into one genuine ample class; decreasing closure and same-class regularization produce the actual extension v_c=v+c log|f| on Y_f and minus infinity on Z(f).

To remove c, use smooth EP rather than asserting these functions decrease when c decreases. Put their canonical potentials Q_j in one fixed ample class on the smooth boundary compactification. Genuine tail envelopes (sup_{j≥m}Q_j)* decrease. On Y_f, where a=log|f| is finite, sup_{j≥m}c_j a=c_m max(a,0), including the generally unattained zero value for a<0. The limit is a genuine extension of v with the original upper growth; same-class regularization gives actual AFS.

Removed-set values require more than dense-open equality plus usc. Pull the extension and a given original weak u to the SAME original resolved witness. Every divisorial point of that integral birational witness has generic algebraic support, so nonzero f is nonzero there and the point lies over Y_f. The functions agree at all these points. Near any tested point floor both by the same constant, use the same reference and shared genuine collar, and apply n2's divisorial order in both directions. Let the floor decrease to minus infinity. This identifies every value, including exceptional and removed points. No assertion about lifting arbitrary prescribed divisorial nets is used. This does not establish affine regularization over every completed residue field.

The nonflat norm algebra can independently be audited. Let A be normal integral and B finite integral over A in characteristic zero, with generic field degree d. For finite module generators b_i, generic N(∑T_i b_i) and all characteristic coefficients lie in A[T]: conjugate products are integral, belong to the fraction field, and A[T] is normal. Translation by every module relation, multiplicativity, homogeneity, N(1)=1 and Cayley–Hamilton are generic polynomial identities and hence hold over A. Right exactness of a finite presentation makes them well-defined after specialization to C=B⊗_A H(s), including new fiber relations.

After algebraic closure of H(s), C is a product of local Artinian algebras. Its unit-group norm character is trivial on nilpotent units: finite characteristic-zero logarithms identify that subgroup with an additive vector group, which has no nonconstant invertible polynomial character. On the residue torus, coefficient comparison in P(xy)=P(x)P(y) gives one monomial. Polynomial extension forces nonnegative integer exponents summing to d. Every exponent is STRICTLY positive: otherwise an idempotent zero in that residue factor and one elsewhere would have nonzero norm and would be invertible by its specialized characteristic identity, a contradiction.

Multiplying each character exponent by its finite separable residue degree gives canonical positive integer weights m_y on the actual analytic fiber, with ∑m_y=d. Unique norm extension over complete fields and the sum of residue degrees after splitting prove compatibility with all complete residue-field extensions. On the flat locus they are Artinian length times residue degree; nonflat fiber dimensions are not substituted.

For u=D⁻¹max_i(log|b_i|+w_i), with a constant floor, expand the actual polynomial N(∑T_i b_i)=∑_{|α|=d}a_αT^α. Arbitrary-radius weighted Gauss multiplicativity gives the whole-base formula

∑_y m_yu(y)=D⁻¹max_α(log|a_α|+∑α_iw_i).

For multiplicativity, the lexicographically largest maximal-weight monomials give a unique maximal contribution at their sum exponent; lower-weight terms cannot cancel it. The floor coefficient is nonzero. Polynomial expressions for original base generators allow dominated generator branches to be appended, making the formula actual AFS in the original base ring.

The degree estimate ||Nπa−Nπb||_E≤d||a−b||_{π⁻¹E} proves locally uniform trace convergence for continuous decreasing AFS limits, using Dini only for continuous limits. Continuity for arbitrary continuous inputs follows by uniform density, on compact preimages, of differences of AFS: they form a rational vector lattice, contain constants in restriction and separate seminorms by truncated regular norms; finite maximum/minimum interpolation gives the density proof. Hence a clopen indicator's trace is an integer sum that is LOCALLY constant. Disconnected opens need not share its value.

Exact nonflat diagnostic: A=k[x,y], I=(x,y), B=A⊕Iz inside z²=x has generic degree two, but fiber dimension three at the origin. N(a+uz)=a²−xu² specializes to a(0)², so the single fiber point has canonical weight TWO, not three.

The norm audit does not complete the general weak trace. Its normalized line slice, proper lift to the original witness, local Gauss map t=cz^e, all residue-field refinements and limiting equality still need to be checked together for that input. The embedded radial argument is not automatically accepted after improving smooth membership. No arbitrary-H(s) affine theorem is imported.

notes.detailedSummary: The unchanged original target and full family are preserved. n1–n3 add compact extension/IBP and smooth-gate proof drafts.
